items.headline: Federal Reserve Finalizes Updates to Stress Test Transparency and Capital Requirements
items.summary: The Federal Reserve has finalized two rules aimed at increasing transparency and reducing volatility in capital requirements for large banks. These changes include new public input processes for stress test scenarios and a revised method for calculating capital buffers, while a separate proposal seeks feedback on modeling fee income.

items.headline: Drug Enforcement Administration Revokes Registration of Montana Practitioner
items.summary: The Drug Enforcement Administration issued a decision and order revoking the certificate of registration held by Alexandra R. Lovec, an advanced practice registered nurse located in Ekalaka, Montana, following allegations of issuing prescriptions outside the usual course of professional practice.

items.headline: DEA Revokes Exempt Status for Inactive Butalbital Prescription Products
items.summary: The Drug Enforcement Administration is revoking the exempted status for specific nonnarcotic prescription products listed on its Table of Exempted Prescription Products whose National Drug Codes are inactive because the items are no longer available or the originating company no longer exists.

items.headline: Federal Reserve Board Publishes Results of the 2025 Survey of Consumer Finances
items.summary: The Federal Reserve released findings from the 2025 Survey of Consumer Finances, offering details on assets, borrowing, and banking habits. Alongside the data, the agency published a summary report tracking shifts in income, net worth, and debt.

items.headline: Federal Reserve Approves Isabella Bank Corporation Acquisition and Merger Application
items.summary: The Federal Reserve Board approved an application by Isabella Bank Corporation to acquire Grand River Commerce, Inc. and its subsidiary. The approval also covers the subsequent bank merger and branch operations.

items.headline: DEA Revokes Registrations Held by Vladimir Romaniv, P.A. Following Default Determination
items.summary: The Drug Enforcement Administration issued a decision and order revoking specific DEA registrations held by Vladimir Romaniv, P.A., after determining the registrant was in default for failing to request a hearing and lacked the necessary state authority to handle controlled substances.

items.headline: Federal Reserve Ends Enforcement Actions for Kansas Financial Institutions
items.summary: The Federal Reserve concluded previous regulatory orders involving a bank holding company and its subsidiary bank in Kansas, ending multiple cease and desist directives and a corrective action directive.

items.headline: Justice and Labor Departments Reach Enforcement Agreement with Cloudera Over PERM Recruitment Allegations
items.summary: The Department of Justice and the Department of Labor announced an enforcement resolution with Cloudera Inc. addressing allegations of discrimination against U.S. workers during PERM recruitment. The resolution includes a debarment, a back-pay fund, civil penalties, and compliance measures.

items.headline: Justice Department Secures Settlement With Lexington Addressing Law Enforcement Practices
items.summary: The Justice Department announced a settlement with the City of Lexington, Mississippi, to address civil rights violations identified in a previous findings report concerning the local police department.

items.headline: New Self-Disclosure Protocol Streamlines Reporting for Health Care Fraud
items.summary: The Department of Justice and the Department of Health and Human Services announced a streamlined self-disclosure policy allowing companies to report potential criminal health care conduct exclusively to the Justice Department to receive benefits from both agencies.

items.headline: Justice Department and FTC File Complaint Against California Ticket Broker Over BOTS Act Violations
items.summary: The Department of Justice and the Federal Trade Commission filed a legal complaint against a California corporation and three of its executives, alleging unlawful acquisition and resale of event tickets using prohibited methods.

items.headline: Justice Department Challenges St. Paul and Portland Local Ordinances Concerning Federal Officers
items.summary: The Department of Justice announced the filing of lawsuits against the cities of St. Paul and Portland, contesting local ordinances that restrict federal law enforcement officers from wearing masks and mandate specific identification protocols.

items.headline: Kansas Health Care Software Company Owner Sentenced to Prison for Fraud Scheme
items.summary: The Department of Justice announced that a Kansas chief executive officer was sentenced to prison for operating an internet platform that produced fraudulent doctors’ orders and prescriptions, resulting in billings of over $1 billion to Medicare and other federal health benefit programs.

items.headline: Somerset Lifesciences Agrees to Four Million Dollar Settlement Over Medicare Claims
items.summary: Somerset Lifesciences Inc. reached an agreement with the Department of Justice to pay four million dollars to resolve claims involving Medicare Part D payments for its generic drug Olopatadine after a brand name equivalent transitioned to over-the-counter status.

items.headline: Department of Justice Secures Settlement From Mortgage Servicer Over Servicemembers Civil Relief Act Violations
items.summary: The Department of Justice announced a settlement requiring a mortgage servicer to pay financial penalties and compensation to resolve allegations of violating federal laws protecting military members, including failing to apply required interest rate caps and engaging in retaliatory actions.

items.headline: Justice Department and Education Department Reach Settlement With UNC to Resolve Discrimination Investigations
items.summary: The U.S. Department of Justice and the Department of Education announced a voluntary settlement agreement with the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill to address concerns regarding antisemitism and race discrimination under federal civil rights laws.

items.headline: Department of Justice and EEOC Secure Joint Settlement With Delivery Service
items.summary: The Department of Justice and the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission announced a joint settlement with Maplebear Inc., doing business as Instacart, addressing allegations of discrimination against workers based on citizenship status and national origin.

items.headline: American Citizen Pleads Guilty to Multi-Year Military Identity Theft Scheme
items.summary: A U.S. citizen has entered a guilty plea for operating an international identity theft and fraud scheme that compromised the bank accounts and benefits of thousands of military-affiliated individuals from overseas.

items.headline: Department of Justice Secures Denaturalization of Two Individuals
items.summary: The Department of Justice reported the removal of U.S. citizenship from two people following federal court orders. Officials stated the individuals obtained citizenship by withholding information regarding past illegal actions during their application processes.

items.headline: Justice Department Resolves Zoning Claims With New York Village
items.summary: The Department of Justice reached a settlement with the Village of Atlantic Beach to address claims that local zoning regulations subjected religious land uses to stricter standards than secular gathering places, violating federal law.

items.headline: Federal Appeals Court Upholds Permit for South Carolina Housing Project
items.summary: The Department of Justice announced that a federal appeals court upheld a Clean Water Act permit issued by the Army Corps of Engineers for a housing development project in Charleston, South Carolina, following a legal defense by department attorneys.

items.headline: Department of Justice Announces Health Care Fraud Charges Against 15 Defendants in Los Angeles
items.summary: The Department of Justice announced charges against 15 defendants, including six medical professionals, involving health care fraud schemes totaling over $1.8 billion in fraudulent claims. The cases include operations related to substance abuse treatment, unnecessary surgical procedures, and hospice care.

items.headline: Department of Justice Extradites Chinese National for Cryptocurrency Scam
items.summary: The Department of Justice announced the arraignment of a Chinese national following his extradition from the Netherlands regarding an international cryptocurrency scam targeting individuals in the United States.

items.headline: DEA Revokes Controlled Substances Registration for Peter Michael Wills, D.D.S.
items.summary: The Drug Enforcement Administration issued a decision and order revoking the federal controlled substances registration held by Peter Michael Wills, D.D.S., of Middletown, Ohio, after determining he lacked the required state authorization and failed to request a hearing.

items.headline: DEA Revokes Registration for Jefferson Burroughs, M.D. Following State License Expiration
items.summary: The Drug Enforcement Administration issued a decision and order revoking the federal registration of Jefferson Burroughs, M.D., after determining that the practitioner lacks the required state medical license and authorization to handle controlled substances.

items.headline: Drug Enforcement Administration Revokes Dental Registration Following State License Expiration
items.summary: The Drug Enforcement Administration issued a decision and order revoking the federal controlled substances registration of a dentist from Ohio after finding that the practitioner no longer holds a valid state dental license or authority to handle controlled substances.

items.headline: DEA Revokes Registration of California Practitioner Following State License Loss
items.summary: The Drug Enforcement Administration announced the revocation of a medical practitioner's certificate of registration after determining she lacked the necessary state authorization to handle controlled substances following the revocation of her state medical license.

items.headline: Federal Agency Revokes Registration for Practitioner Lacking State Medical License
items.summary: The Drug Enforcement Administration issued a decision and order to revoke a medical registration after finding the holder lacked active licensing and failed to respond to administrative notices.

items.headline: Drug Enforcement Administration Revokes Registration of Washington Practitioner
items.summary: The Drug Enforcement Administration announced the revocation of a Washington practitioner's registration following the suspension of her state medical license and her resulting lack of authority to handle controlled substances.

items.headline: Justice Department and HHS Launch Healthcare False Claims Act Self-Disclosure Pilot Program
items.summary: The Department of Justice Civil Division and the Department of Health and Human Services announced a joint pilot program allowing healthcare companies to self-disclose potential False Claims Act violations, aiming to streamline resolutions and focus enforcement resources.

items.headline: Ukrainian National Sentenced for Role in Global Ransomware Conspiracies
items.summary: The Department of Justice announced that a Ukrainian national received a prison sentence for participating in computer fraud conspiracies involving ransomware attacks against international businesses, government entities, and healthcare facilities.

items.headline: Contractor Admits Guilt in Kickback Scheme Involving Postal Service Repairs
items.summary: The Department of Justice announced that an Oregon contractor pleaded guilty to participating in a conspiracy involving more than $465,000 in illegal kickbacks related to repair work on federal postal facilities.

items.headline: Former Army Official Pleads Guilty to Defense Contract Bribery and Fraud
items.summary: The Department of Justice announced that a former civilian United States Army official pleaded guilty to conspiracy, bribery, and major fraud charges related to defense contracts in Hawaii.

items.headline: Miami Tax Return Preparer Permanently Barred from Industry by Court Order
items.summary: The Department of Justice announced that a federal court issued a permanent injunction against a Miami area tax return preparer, prohibiting him from preparing returns, advising clients, or operating a tax preparation business.

items.headline: Department of Justice Refers Asphalt Industry Merger Investigations to State Attorneys General
items.summary: The Department of Justice Antitrust Division announced the successful referral of two separate asphalt industry merger investigations to state attorneys general, leading to coordinated settlements and facility divestitures in multiple states.

items.headline: Federal Reserve Maintains Federal Funds Rate Target Range
items.summary: The Federal Open Market Committee voted to keep the federal funds rate target range steady while noting strong economic expansion, robust capital investment, and elevated inflation.

items.headline: Department of Justice Announces Sentences in International Smuggling and Fraud Case
items.summary: The Department of Justice announced that five Cuban nationals and one U.S. citizen received prison sentences for participating in an international alien smuggling, asylum fraud, and money laundering conspiracy that moved individuals into the United States and laundered millions of dollars.

items.headline: Former U.S. Postal Service Official Enters Guilty Plea in Connection with Multi-Million Dollar Contracting Bribery Scheme
items.summary: The Department of Justice reported that a former procurement official for the U.S. Postal Service pleaded guilty to charges involving bribery and honest services wire fraud after manipulating the contract awarding process.

items.headline: Department of Justice Details Collaboration with State Attorneys General on Local Merger Reviews
items.summary: The Department of Justice shared an update concerning the Antitrust Division's cooperative efforts with state Attorneys General in evaluating corporate mergers primarily affecting local jurisdictions. The update outlines how federal and state enforcers divide merger investigations based on regional and national interests.
